lambda_c_alpha4.cite: Spiked Wishart threshold at alpha = m/n = 4 with unit-variance priors. Baik, Ben Arous & Peche, 'Phase transition of the largest eigenvalue for non-null complex sample covariance matrices', Ann. Probab. 33, 1643 (2005), arXiv:math/0403022v2 (PDF read), Theorem 1.1 (36): the critical population eigenvalue l_c = 1 + gamma^(-1) with M/N = gamma^2 (complex samples; Sec. 1.3 conjectures the same critical value for real samples); Lesieur, Krzakala & Zdeborova, J. Stat. Mech. (2017) 073403, arXiv:1701.00858v1 (PDF read), Eq. (198): the uniform fixed point of the bipartite SE is stable for Delta > Delta_c = sqrt(alpha) lambda_max(Sigma_u Sigma_v) (= sqrt(alpha) for unit variances; 'this criteria agrees with the criteria for spectral phase transition'). Convention (inference/wishart.py): replicant's Y = (lambda/n) u v^T + W, W_ij ~ N(0, 1/n), is LKZ's Y/sqrt(N Delta) with lambda = 1/sqrt(Delta), so lambda_c = alpha^(-1/4) = 2^(-1/2) (exact); with v Gaussian the columns of sqrt(n) Y are samples of covariance I + lambda^2 uhat uhat^T: BBP's N = n, M = m, gamma^2 = alpha, l_1 = 1 + lambda^2, and l_c gives the same lambda_c. The notes' (12.87) lambda_notes = lambda^2 = alpha^(-1/2) = 1/2 at this point. tol 1e-9 is the accuracy of the numerical route
